title: Patterns solve repeated problems
summary: A pattern gives a name to a useful design idea. Before choosing one, describe the job the code must do.
introduction: A pattern gives a name to a useful design idea. Before choosing one, describe the job the code must do. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A pattern gives a name to a useful design idea. Before choosing one, describe the job the code must do.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Run the JavaScript examples here. Choose a pattern only when it makes a real problem easier to understand.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Design Patterns. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
const job = { input: 3, action: n => n * 2 };
console.log(job.action(job.input));
blocks.title: Patterns solve repeated problems

blocks.text: The result is 6. A tiny function already solves this job; no extra class is needed.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Adding a pattern without a problem can make simple code harder.
For more detail later, use this [Design Patterns further reading](https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns).
